newsitem.title: USA: CBOT May contracts expire quietly, oats settle up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT May contracts expire quietly, oats settle up.

text.p: CBOT May agricultural futures contracts expired quietly at 1201 CDT Tuesday with May oats going off the board sharply higher, traders said.
The May oat contract settled at $1.76 per bushel, up 7-3/4 cents after trading 10-3/4 cents higher during the expiration.
Firm cash oat markets and talk of delays in importing oats from Scandinavian countries kept a firm undertone to the oat markets, trade sources said.

Rand Financial sold 150,000 bushels of the May during the close on a market-on-close order and dropped the contract from the daily high which also was the expiration high of $1.79 per bushel. ADM Investor Services sold 50,000 bushels of the May just prior to expiration, traders said.

May soymeal expired quietly despite some early concerns that that contract could undergo violent gyrations during expiration. The open interest in the May early Tuesday was at a level considered a bit steep for the eve of expiration, traders said.
May meal expired $1.90 per ton lower at $304.50 per ton. Smith Barney was an outright purchaser of the May and the key bull spreader of 30 May/July at $15.00 per ton, premium May, traders said.
Tenco Inc spread 25 May/July at $15.50 per ton, premium May, traders said. Rand Financial, ADM Investor Services and Prudential Securites were spreading the July/May, traders said.

May soybeans settled at $8.64-3/4, down 2-3/4. Rand Financial spread one million bushels of July/May at two cents, premium May and Central Soya spread 200,000 bushels of May/July at three cents, premium May, traders said.
May soyoil expired quietly at 23.51 cents per lb, down 0.04 cent per lb.

May corn expired 5-1/2 cents per bushel lower at $2.87-3/4. LIT America bought 200,000 bushels of May during expiration and Continental Grain, earlier in the session, was a key bear spreader of one million bushels of July/May at nine cents, premium, May, traders said.
In wheat, the May expired 11 cents per bushel lower at $3.81. Merrill Lynch Futures was a key seller of the May during expiration, traders said.
